cap: The head passes the pelvis in six cardinal movements: engagement, descent with flexion, internal rotation, extension, external rotation (restitution) and expulsion of the shoulders. If the anterior shoulder catches behind the symphysis, lateral traction on the head stretches the upper trunk, C5 and C6, causing Erb palsy with a waiter's tip arm. Traction on an arm above the head stretches the lower trunk, C8 and T1, causing Klumpke palsy, a claw hand with possible Horner syndrome.
